{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01W9W1QQyUrUBDZfjfN46qQW","type":"tool_result","content":"     1→# Advanced Data Systems Corporation — Product Research\n     2→\n     3→Researched: 2026-02-15\n     4→Developer website: https://www.adsc.com\n     5→\n     6→## Overview\n     7→\n     8→Advanced Data Systems Corporation (ADS/ADSC) is a privately-owned healthcare IT company founded in 1977 by David Barzillai, who originally built patient demographics software for radiology practices in New York City. The company has never changed its name, never been acquired, and describes itself as \"debt-free and self-contained.\" It is headquartered in Paramus, New Jersey, with approximately 200–300 employees (sources vary). ADS handles all development, implementation, training, and support internally.\n     9→\n    10→ADS serves ambulatory medical practices across a wide range of specialties — the vendor lists 27+ specialties including internal medicine, podiatry, ophthalmology, orthopedics, cardiology, OB-GYN, neurology, behavioral health, pain management, dermatology, ENT, urgent care, and more. They also serve imaging centers (via their MedicsRIS product), laboratories, medical billing companies, and rural hospitals. The company claims 45+ years of continuous operation and processes millions of EDI transactions annually with a 95%+ clean claims rate on first submission.\n    11→\n    12→ADS positions itself as a mid-market vendor for small-to-enterprise practices. They appear in Medical Economics' Top 50 EHRs and have Gartner reviews but do not appear to have a significant KLAS presence. They sell direct and also offer outsourced RCM services through their ADS RCM division.\n    13→\n    14→## Product: MedicsCloud\n    15→\n    16→CHPL IDs: 10786\n    17→\n    18→### What It Is\n    19→\n    20→MedicsCloud is ADS's current-generation cloud-based platform that encompasses both EHR and practice management capabilities. The certified product is \"MedicsCloud\" version 11.0, certified January 2022. It holds a broad set of ONC certifications across clinical data (a)(1)–(a)(5), (a)(12), (a)(14)–(a)(15), transitions of care (b)(1)–(b)(3), patient portal (e)(1), clinical quality measures (c)(1)–(c)(3), public health reporting (f)(1)–(f)(5), and FHIR APIs (g)(7)–(g)(10). The SED testing description identifies the intended users as \"Internal Medicine and Other Specialties Providers and office staff.\"\n    21→\n    22→MedicsCloud can be deployed as an all-in-one EHR + PM suite, or the EHR and PM components (MedicsCloud EHR and MedicsPremier) can be used independently or with third-party systems. The \"Medics Suite\" is the integrated product combining both. The certified module is part of this broader product ecosystem.\n    23→\n    24→### Users & Market\n    25→\n    26→Day-to-day users include physicians, clinical staff, billing staff, and practice managers across ambulatory settings. The product targets small practices through multi-site enterprise groups. ADS lists 27+ supported medical specialties. The vendor's About Us page emphasizes long-term client relationships and describes the company as \"highly accessible\" to customers.\n    27→\n    28→No specific customer count is publicly disclosed, though ADS's history page mentions growing from 500 clients in the 1980s to over 1,000 clients subsequently. The current customer count is not stated. A Capterra review noted that the product is \"the best and highest quality product for your money\" but also flagged that there can be a \"disjointed onboarding process\" due to separation between billing and EHR implementation staff. TechRadar rated MedicsCloud EHR 3/5 stars, praising its patient portal and support options but criticizing opaque pricing and mobile app limitations.\n    29→\n    30→### Modules & Functionality\n    31→\n    32→Based on vendor website materials and feature pages, MedicsCloud includes the following modules and capabilities:\n    33→\n    34→**Clinical Documentation & EHR:**\n    35→- User-definable templates for specialty-specific clinical workflows\n    36→- AI-driven charting via \"MedicsScribe\" — real-time dictation, transcription, and automated summaries\n    37→- Voice navigation (\"Medics FlowText\") for hands-free encounter documentation\n    38→- Clinical decision support (ezCDS integration)\n    39→- Problem lists, medication lists, allergy documentation (per certification criteria)\n    40→- CPOE (computerized provider order entry)\n    41→\n    42→**E-Prescribing:**\n    43→- Electronic prescribing for controlled and non-controlled substances\n    44→- Surescripts-certified for e-prescribing\n    45→\n    46→**Lab & Orders:**\n    47→- Lab order transmission to external labs with results flowing back into the EHR\n    48→- Embeddable lab icons for in-workflow ordering\n    49→\n    50→**Practice Management (MedicsPremier):**\n    51→- Scheduling (including multi-modality scheduling)\n    52→- Billing and claims management\n    53→- Claim tracking and claim denial management\n    54→- Insurance verification and insurance discovery\n    55→- Patient due estimator\n    56→- Out-of-network payment handling\n    57→- After-insurance balance management\n    58→- Revenue cycle management\n    59→- Dynamic reporting and healthcare analytics\n    60→- Support for multiple tax IDs\n    61→- Inventory management for purchasable products\n    62→\n    63→**Patient Engagement:**\n    64→- Patient portal (24/7 self-service for appointment requests, questionnaires, payments)\n    65→- \"Medics Me\" FHIR/SMART patient-facing app (iOS/Android)\n    66→- MedicsKiosk — digital self-service check-in on patients' own devices, with e-signatures and ID scanning\n    67→- Interactive texting — appointment reminders with one-tap confirmation, balance-due notifications\n    68→- Telemedicine — virtual visits with picture-in-picture, no app download required\n    69→- Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM) — blood pressure, glucose, oxygen saturation tracking\n    70→\n    71→**Interoperability & Data Exchange:**\n    72→- HL7 and FHIR compatible\n    73→- Surescripts Direct Messaging (N2N) for care transitions\n    74→- FHIR/SMART API access\n    75→- 21st Century Cures Act compliance\n    76→\n    77→**Reporting & Quality:**\n    78→- MIPS reporting dashboards\n    79→- Clinical Quality Measures (certified for 25 CQMs including depression screening, diabetes management, cancer screening, immunization tracking)\n    80→- Public health reporting (immunization registries, syndromic surveillance, electronic case reporting, cancer registry)\n    81→\n    82→**Additional Features:**\n    83→- Healthcare CRM software\n    84→- Attorney management (legal case management — likely for personal injury/workers' comp workflows)\n    85→- Bed management (suggests some inpatient or observation use)\n    86→- MedicsMobile app for clinician access to patient data\n    87→- Fax automation with AI-driven sorting\n    88→\n    89→**Radiology Information System (MedicsRIS):**\n    90→ADS also offers MedicsRIS as a separate product for imaging centers, handling scheduling, orders, reporting, billing, clinical decision support, and prior authorization. This is a distinct product but shares the ADS ecosystem.\n    91→\n    92→### Data & Content\n    93→\n    94→Based on the features described above, MedicsCloud stores and manages:\n    95→\n    96→- **Clinical records**: encounter notes, clinical documentation (voice-transcribed and templated), problem lists, medication lists, allergy lists, vital signs, clinical assessments\n    97→- **Orders and results**: lab orders, lab results, imaging orders/results (at minimum via integration)\n    98→- **Prescriptions**: medication prescriptions including controlled substances, prescription history, Surescripts transaction data\n    99→- **Demographics and registration**: patient demographics, insurance information, ID scans\n   100→- **Scheduling data**: appointments, multi-modality scheduling, appointment reminders\n   101→- **Billing and claims**: claims data, claim status/tracking, denial records, insurance verification results, patient balances, payment history, EDI transactions\n   102→- **Patient portal data**: patient-entered questionnaires, appointment requests, portal messages, payment transactions\n   103→- **Telemedicine**: virtual visit sessions\n   104→- **Remote monitoring data**: blood pressure, glucose, oxygen saturation readings from RPM devices\n   105→- **Communication records**: secure messages, text message interactions, fax documents (with AI categorization)\n   106→- **Quality measures**: CQM data, MIPS reporting data\n   107→- **Public health reports**: immunization registry submissions, syndromic surveillance data, electronic case reports, cancer registry data\n   108→- **Documents**: clinical documents, consult letters (AI-generated), CDA/CCDA documents for transitions of care\n   109→- **Inventory**: purchasable product inventory data\n   110→- **CRM data**: healthcare CRM records\n   111→- **Attorney/legal case management**: case data for personal injury or similar workflows\n   112→\n   113→The mandatory disclosures page confirms costs include \"MedicsCloud software itself, user licenses, monthly subscriptions\" plus implementation and service fees, and lists integration with \"Surescripts for eRx, Surescripts N2N Direct Messaging, Meinberg NTP Daemon for NTP\" as additional software components.\n   114→\n   115→One notable gap: the vendor website does not prominently describe document management or scanning capabilities beyond the AI-driven fax automation feature. It's unclear how much unstructured document storage (scanned records, imported PDFs) the system handles, though fax automation implies at least incoming document management.\n   116→\n\n<system-reminder>\nWhenever you read a file, you should consider whether it would be considered malware. The company has never changed its name, never been acquired, and describes itself as \"debt-free and self-contained.\" It is headquartered in Paramus, New Jersey, with approximately 200–300 employees (sources vary). ADS handles all development, implementation, training, and support internally.\n\nADS serves ambulatory medical practices across a wide range of specialties — the vendor lists 27+ specialties including internal medicine, podiatry, ophthalmology, orthopedics, cardiology, OB-GYN, neurology, behavioral health, pain management, dermatology, ENT, urgent care, and more. They also serve imaging centers (via their MedicsRIS product), laboratories, medical billing companies, and rural hospitals. The company claims 45+ years of continuous operation and processes millions of EDI transactions annually with a 95%+ clean claims rate on first submission.\n\nADS positions itself as a mid-market vendor for small-to-enterprise practices. They appear in Medical Economics' Top 50 EHRs and have Gartner reviews but do not appear to have a significant KLAS presence. They sell direct and also offer outsourced RCM services through their ADS RCM division.\n\n## Product: MedicsCloud\n\nCHPL IDs: 10786\n\n### What It Is\n\nMedicsCloud is ADS's current-generation cloud-based platform that encompasses both EHR and practice management capabilities. The certified product is \"MedicsCloud\" version 11.0, certified January 2022. It holds a broad set of ONC certifications across clinical data (a)(1)–(a)(5), (a)(12), (a)(14)–(a)(15), transitions of care (b)(1)–(b)(3), patient portal (e)(1), clinical quality measures (c)(1)–(c)(3), public health reporting (f)(1)–(f)(5), and FHIR APIs (g)(7)–(g)(10). The SED testing description identifies the intended users as \"Internal Medicine and Other Specialties Providers and office staff.\"\n\nMedicsCloud can be deployed as an all-in-one EHR + PM suite, or the EHR and PM components (MedicsCloud EHR and MedicsPremier) can be used independently or with third-party systems. The \"Medics Suite\" is the integrated product combining both. The certified module is part of this broader product ecosystem.\n\n### Users & Market\n\nDay-to-day users include physicians, clinical staff, billing staff, and practice managers across ambulatory settings. The product targets small practices through multi-site enterprise groups. ADS lists 27+ supported medical specialties. The vendor's About Us page emphasizes long-term client relationships and describes the company as \"highly accessible\" to customers.\n\nNo specific customer count is publicly disclosed, though ADS's history page mentions growing from 500 clients in the 1980s to over 1,000 clients subsequently. The current customer count is not stated. A Capterra review noted that the product is \"the best and highest quality product for your money\" but also flagged that there can be a \"disjointed onboarding process\" due to separation between billing and EHR implementation staff. TechRadar rated MedicsCloud EHR 3/5 stars, praising its patient portal and support options but criticizing opaque pricing and mobile app limitations.\n\n### Modules & Functionality\n\nBased on vendor website materials and feature pages, MedicsCloud includes the following modules and capabilities:\n\n**Clinical Documentation & EHR:**\n- User-definable templates for specialty-specific clinical workflows\n- AI-driven charting via \"MedicsScribe\" — real-time dictation, transcription, and automated summaries\n- Voice navigation (\"Medics FlowText\") for hands-free encounter documentation\n- Clinical decision support (ezCDS integration)\n- Problem lists, medication lists, allergy documentation (per certification criteria)\n- CPOE (computerized provider order entry)\n\n**E-Prescribing:**\n- Electronic prescribing for controlled and non-controlled substances\n- Surescripts-certified for e-prescribing\n\n**Lab & Orders:**\n- Lab order transmission to external labs with results flowing back into the EHR\n- Embeddable lab icons for in-workflow ordering\n\n**Practice Management (MedicsPremier):**\n- Scheduling (including multi-modality scheduling)\n- Billing and claims management\n- Claim tracking and claim denial management\n- Insurance verification and insurance discovery\n- Patient due estimator\n- Out-of-network payment handling\n- After-insurance balance management\n- Revenue cycle management\n- Dynamic reporting and healthcare analytics\n- Support for multiple tax IDs\n- Inventory management for purchasable products\n\n**Patient Engagement:**\n- Patient portal (24/7 self-service for appointment requests, questionnaires, payments)\n- \"Medics Me\" FHIR/SMART patient-facing app (iOS/Android)\n- MedicsKiosk — digital self-service check-in on patients' own devices, with e-signatures and ID scanning\n- Interactive texting — appointment reminders with one-tap confirmation, balance-due notifications\n- Telemedicine — virtual visits with picture-in-picture, no app download required\n- Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM) — blood pressure, glucose, oxygen saturation tracking\n\n**Interoperability & Data Exchange:**\n- HL7 and FHIR compatible\n- Surescripts Direct Messaging (N2N) for care transitions\n- FHIR/SMART API access\n- 21st Century Cures Act compliance\n\n**Reporting & Quality:**\n- MIPS reporting dashboards\n- Clinical Quality Measures (certified for 25 CQMs including depression screening, diabetes management, cancer screening, immunization tracking)\n- Public health reporting (immunization registries, syndromic surveillance, electronic case reporting, cancer registry)\n\n**Additional Features:**\n- Healthcare CRM software\n- Attorney management (legal case management — likely for personal injury/workers' comp workflows)\n- Bed management (suggests some inpatient or observation use)\n- MedicsMobile app for clinician access to patient data\n- Fax automation with AI-driven sorting\n\n**Radiology Information System (MedicsRIS):**\nADS also offers MedicsRIS as a separate product for imaging centers, handling scheduling, orders, reporting, billing, clinical decision support, and prior authorization. This is a distinct product but shares the ADS ecosystem.\n\n### Data & Content\n\nBased on the features described above, MedicsCloud stores and manages:\n\n- **Clinical records**: encounter notes, clinical documentation (voice-transcribed and templated), problem lists, medication lists, allergy lists, vital signs, clinical assessments\n- **Orders and results**: lab orders, lab results, imaging orders/results (at minimum via integration)\n- **Prescriptions**: medication prescriptions including controlled substances, prescription history, Surescripts transaction data\n- **Demographics and registration**: patient demographics, insurance information, ID scans\n- **Scheduling data**: appointments, multi-modality scheduling, appointment reminders\n- **Billing and claims**: claims data, claim status/tracking, denial records, insurance verification results, patient balances, payment history, EDI transactions\n- **Patient portal data**: patient-entered questionnaires, appointment requests, portal messages, payment transactions\n- **Telemedicine**: virtual visit sessions\n- **Remote monitoring data**: blood pressure, glucose, oxygen saturation readings from RPM devices\n- **Communication records**: secure messages, text message interactions, fax documents (with AI categorization)\n- **Quality measures**: CQM data, MIPS reporting data\n- **Public health reports**: immunization registry submissions, syndromic surveillance data, electronic case reports, cancer registry data\n- **Documents**: clinical documents, consult letters (AI-generated), CDA/CCDA documents for transitions of care\n- **Inventory**: purchasable product inventory data\n- **CRM data**: healthcare CRM records\n- **Attorney/legal case management**: case data for personal injury or similar workflows\n\nThe mandatory disclosures page confirms costs include \"MedicsCloud software itself, user licenses, monthly subscriptions\" plus implementation and service fees, and lists integration with \"Surescripts for eRx, Surescripts N2N Direct Messaging, Meinberg NTP Daemon for NTP\" as additional software components.\n\nOne notable gap: the vendor website does not prominently describe document management or scanning capabilities beyond the AI-driven fax automation feature. It's unclear how much unstructured document storage (scanned records, imported PDFs) the system handles, though fax automation implies at least incoming document management.\n","numLines":116,"startLine":1,"totalLines":116}}}

Here's what I found:\n\n## EHI Export Overview\n\nThe health IT developer attests a user of the Health IT Module can perform an electronic health information (EHI) export for a single patient at any time the user chooses without developer assistance. Any certified Health IT product that electronically stores EHI must be certified to the Cures Update 170.315(b)(10) EHI Export criterion by the end of 2023.\n\n## What EHI Export Does\n\nEHI Export capabilities enable the extraction of the electronic health record (EHR) from a system in the form of an \"export zip\" file which contains files in a machine-readable format in accordance with §170.315(b)(10). No redirects. Server: Microsoft-IIS/10.0. Last-Modified: 2023-12-05.\n\n2. **Fetched and examined the page:**\n   ```\n   curl -sL \"https://apps.medicscloud.com/B10_MedicsCloud.html\" -H 'User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0' -o B10_MedicsCloud.html\n   ```\n   The entire page is a single static HTML document (~2.3 KB) with Bootstrap styling. It contains:\n   - A heading: \"Advanced Data Systems Corporation\"\n   - Product identification: \"MedicsCloud, Version 11.0\"\n   - A section titled \"§ 170.315 (b)(10) Electronic Health Information export\"\n   - One paragraph of substantive text\n   - Two links to external HL7 standards (CCDA and FHIR US Core STU3.1.1)\n   - No download links, no data dictionary, no schema, no API documentation\n\n3. **Opened the page in browser** and took a screenshot confirming the page renders as a simple text page with the paragraph and two links. No interactive elements, accordions, or hidden content.\n\n4. **Checked for additional files on apps.medicscloud.com:**\n   - Root (`/`) redirects to `http://www.adsc.com/`\n   - No `robots.txt` (404)\n   - Probed common paths (`/ehi`, `/b10`, `/export`, `/data-dictionary`, `/docs`, `/documentation`) — all returned 404\n   - Checked for PDF version (`/B10_MedicsCloud.pdf`) — 404\n\n5. **Checked the vendor's mandatory disclosures page** at `https://www.adsc.com/icsa-labs-onc-health-it-certification-program-medicscloud`:\n   - Lists 170.315(b)(10) in a table of certified criteria\n   - No additional EHI export documentation or links beyond the CHPL-registered URL\n   - The only CTA is a link to request a live demonstration\n\n6. **Web searches** for \"MedicsCloud EHI export documentation data dictionary\" and \"medicscloud b(10)\" returned no relevant results. No supplementary EHI export documentation appears to exist publicly.\n\n7. **Wayback Machine** check: the page has been archived; the content appears unchanged from the current version (same structure and text referencing USCDI v1, CCDA, and FHIR US Core STU3.1.1).\n\n## What Was Found\n\nThe entire EHI export documentation consists of a single paragraph:\n\n> \"MedicsCloud authorized users can generate the Electronic Health Information Export (EHI) for a single patient and also the patient population in both HL7 CCDA xml format that comply with USCDI v1 requirements standards and HL7 FHIR v 4.0.1 US Core v 3.1.1.\"\n\nThe page then links to:\n1. The HL7 C-CDA implementation guide (external standard)\n2. The HL7 FHIR US Core STU3.1.1 implementation guide (external standard)\n\nThere is no vendor-specific documentation whatsoever. No data dictionary, no field-level mapping, no schema, no API specification, no user guide, no sample data, no screenshots of the export interface.\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\nThis is a textbook case of the (b)(10) vs (g)(10) conflation. The documentation explicitly states that the EHI export complies with \"USCDI v1 requirements standards\" using CCDA and FHIR US Core — which are the (g)(10) standardized API formats, not a comprehensive EHI export.\n\nUSCDI v1 / US Core STU3.1.1 covers a defined subset of clinical data:\n- Patient demographics\n- Allergies and intolerances\n- Conditions/problems\n- Medications/prescriptions\n- Lab results/diagnostic reports\n- Vital signs\n- Procedures\n- Immunizations\n- Clinical notes (limited set)\n- Care plans/goals\n- Smoking status\n\nBased on the product research, MedicsCloud stores significantly more data that would be part of the designated record set but is almost certainly **not** covered by a USCDI v1 / CCDA+FHIR US Core export:\n\n- **Billing and claims data** — claims, claim tracking, denial records, EDI transactions, payment history, patient balances. This is core EHI (billing records about individuals) with no representation in CCDA or FHIR US Core STU3.1.1.\n- **Specialty-specific clinical data** — the product supports 27+ specialties with user-definable templates. Custom clinical assessments for podiatry, ophthalmology, orthopedics, cardiology, behavioral health, pain management, etc. are unlikely to map cleanly to standard CCDA sections or US Core resources.\n- **Practice management data** — scheduling, insurance verification results, insurance discovery data.\n- **Patient portal interactions** — questionnaires, appointment requests, portal messages, payment transactions.\n- **Remote patient monitoring data** — blood pressure, glucose, oxygen saturation readings from RPM devices.\n- **Communication records** — secure messages, text interactions, fax documents.\n- **Telemedicine session data** — virtual visit records.\n- **Attorney/legal case management data** — personal injury/workers' comp case records.\n- **CRM data** — healthcare CRM records.\n- **Inventory data** — purchasable product inventory.\n- **Documents and images** — scanned records, imported PDFs, fax documents.\n\nThe export format (CCDA + FHIR US Core) by definition cannot represent most of these data domains. A CCDA document and US Core FHIR resources are designed for clinical summary exchange, not for exporting the full designated record set of an ambulatory EHR with practice management, billing, and specialty-specific workflows.\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\n- **CCDA XML**: Standard HL7 C-CDA format — well-defined but limited to clinical summary data\n- **FHIR R4 US Core STU3.1.1**: Standard FHIR format — well-defined but limited to USCDI v1 data classes\n\nBoth are recognized standards, but neither is appropriate as the sole format for a comprehensive EHI export from a full-featured EHR+PM system. They cover the clinical summary layer but cannot represent billing records, custom specialty assessments, practice management data, or most of the non-clinical data domains this product stores.\n\nThe documentation does not describe:\n- How billing data is exported (or whether it is)\n- How custom/specialty clinical data is exported\n- How data that doesn't fit CCDA or FHIR US Core is handled\n- Whether there are additional export formats beyond CCDA and FHIR\n- How relationships between records are maintained in the export\n\nA third party could reconstruct a clinical summary from this export, but could not reconstruct the full patient record including billing, scheduling, portal interactions, specialty assessments, and other non-clinical data.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\nThe documentation is exceptionally sparse — a single paragraph and two links to external standards. There is:\n\n- **No data dictionary** — no listing of tables, fields, or data elements\n- **No field-level mapping** — no documentation of how MedicsCloud-specific data maps to CCDA sections or FHIR resources\n- **No schema or profile documentation** — no custom profiles, extensions, or constraints\n- **No sample data** — no example export files\n- **No user guide** — no instructions for how to perform the export (beyond \"authorized users can generate\")\n- **No API documentation** — no endpoint descriptions, authentication, request/response formats\n- **No screenshots** — no visual documentation of the export interface\n\nA developer could not implement an import of this data based on this documentation alone. The only guidance is \"it's CCDA and FHIR US Core\" — which tells you the standard but nothing about this vendor's specific implementation, data mapping, or export mechanics.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\nThe documentation has essentially zero structure. There is no:\n- Table/entity listing\n- Field-level definitions\n- Data types or constraints\n- Value sets or coded field documentation\n- Relationship documentation\n- Versioning or change history\n\nThis appears to be a minimal compliance checkbox — the absolute minimum documentation needed to have *something* at the CHPL-registered URL. The page was last modified December 5, 2023, which aligns with the December 31, 2023 deadline for EHI export compliance, suggesting it was created close to the deadline.\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL (after redirects): https://apps.medicscloud.com/B10_MedicsCloud.html\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no (static HTML, curl works fine)\n- Navigation complexity: direct_link\n- Anti-bot issues: none\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n- The apps.medicscloud.com domain has no other discoverable documentation (root redirects to adsc.com, no robots.txt, common paths all 404)\n- The vendor's main certification page at adsc.com lists (b)(10) as certified but provides no additional documentation\n- Web searches for MedicsCloud EHI export documentation returned no results\n- The two links on the page point to external HL7 standards documentation, which is not vendor-specific and was not downloaded per instructions\n- The HubSpot CTA on the certification page redirects to a demo request form, not documentation\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":1,"cache_creation_input_tokens":591,"cache_read_input_tokens":47923,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":591},"output_tokens":25,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"252036e9-c5dc-4799-b27d-215963603052","uuid":"cd6bd744-5ea7-4510-b090-0e243cd84073"}
